scenes.tts: Press a fingertip and hold it. Is that one signal reaching your brain, or several?
scenes.visual: A fingertip under a smooth probe. Title card: One press, several reports.
scenes.narration: Press a fingertip and hold it. Is that one signal reaching your brain, or several?

scenes.tts: In Touch and pain, you sorted four touch afferents of the hand into a two by two table. You used firing alone.
scenes.visual: The Touch and pain table flashes in: slowly or rapidly adapting, small or large receptive field. Label: what you already know.
scenes.caption: In Touch and pain, you sorted four touch afferents of the hand into a two-by-two table. You used firing alone.
scenes.narration: In Touch and pain, you sorted four touch afferents of the hand into a two-by-two table. You used firing alone.

scenes.tts: So what lies behind each box? And why split one touch into several signals at all?
scenes.visual: Question marks appear over each box of the table.
scenes.narration: So what lies behind each box? And why split one touch into several signals at all?

scenes.tts: Start simple. A smooth probe presses into a fingertip, holds still for a second, then lifts.
scenes.visual: A position trace draws beneath the fingertip: ramp in, hold, ramp out. Labels: press, hold, lift.
scenes.narration: Start simple. A smooth probe presses into a fingertip, holds still for a second, then lifts.

scenes.tts: Record from each kind of touch afferent in turn, and line up its spikes under the probe.
scenes.visual: Three empty raster rows appear beneath the position trace, labelled SA I, RA and PC.
scenes.narration: Record from each kind of touch afferent in turn, and line up its spikes under the probe.

scenes.tts: Which afferent keeps firing while the probe is held still?
scenes.visual: The hold segment of the trace is highlighted. On screen: which one keeps firing?
scenes.narration: Which afferent keeps firing while the probe is held still?

scenes.visual: The question stays on screen; a small countdown ring runs.

scenes.tts: The slowly adapting afferent that ends at Merkel cells. It fires going in, and keeps firing through the hold.
scenes.visual: The SA I row fills: spikes at the press and all through the hold. Label: slowly adapting, Merkel cells.
scenes.narration: The slowly adapting afferent that ends at Merkel cells. It fires going in, and keeps firing through the hold.

scenes.tts: It reports that something is there, and where its edges are.
scenes.visual: A coin-shaped outline appears under the probe, its edges highlighted.
scenes.narration: It reports that something is there, and where its edges are.

scenes.tts: The rapidly adapting afferent in a Meissner corpuscle fires going in, and again on lifting. During the hold, it is quiet.
scenes.visual: The RA row fills: a burst at the press, silence in the hold, a burst at the lift. Label: rapidly adapting, Meissner corpuscle.
scenes.narration: The rapidly adapting afferent in a Meissner corpuscle fires going in, and again on lifting. During the hold, it is quiet.

scenes.tts: The Pa sinny an afferent is silent during the hold. At most, it gives a brief burst as the probe goes in and lifts.
scenes.visual: The PC row shows a few transient spikes at the press and at the lift, and nothing in the hold. Label: Pacinian.
scenes.narration: The Pacinian afferent is silent during the hold. At most, it gives a brief burst as the probe goes in and lifts.
scenes.caption: The Pacinian afferent is silent during the hold. At most, it gives a brief burst as the probe goes in and lifts.

scenes.tts: Now make the probe vibrate fast, with tiny movements. Which afferent detects the smallest vibration?
scenes.visual: The probe trace turns into a fast, small oscillation whose size grows slowly from nothing. On screen: 250 Hz.
scenes.narration: Now make the probe vibrate fast, with tiny movements. Which afferent detects the smallest vibration?

scenes.visual: The question stays on screen; a small countdown ring runs.

scenes.tts: The Pa sinny an afferent. It is the most sensitive to fast vibration. The slowly adapting afferent hardly responds.
scenes.visual: The PC row fills densely; the SA I row stays nearly empty. On screen: Pacinian best near 100 to 300 Hz.
scenes.narration: The Pacinian afferent. It is the most sensitive to fast vibration. The slowly adapting afferent hardly responds.
scenes.caption: The Pacinian afferent. It is the most sensitive to fast vibration. The slowly adapting afferent hardly responds.

scenes.tts: Each class has a band where it is most sensitive. A band of best sensitivity, not a cutoff.
scenes.visual: Schematic overlapping sensitivity curves, one per afferent, labelled 'relative sensitivity, schematic': SA I extends down to the held press, RA peaks at lower frequencies, PC near 250 Hz.
scenes.narration: Each class has a band where it is most sensitive. A band of best sensitivity, not a cutoff.

scenes.tts: Same skin, same probe, different records. Each is one part of the touch.
scenes.visual: The three rasters stack under one probe trace.
scenes.narration: Same skin, same probe, different records. Each is one part of the touch.

scenes.tts: Here is the one idea to carry. Each class of low threshold mechano receptor is most sensitive to a different part of a touch.
scenes.visual: Callout card: The one idea. Each LTMR class is most sensitive to a different part of a touch.
scenes.caption: Here is the one idea to carry. Each class of low-threshold mechanoreceptor is most sensitive to a different part of a touch.
scenes.narration: Here is the one idea to carry. Each class of low-threshold mechanoreceptor is most sensitive to a different part of a touch.

scenes.tts: Like overlapping filters, each class favours its own part. A held press. Skin motion. Fast vibration. The slightest bend of a hair. A slow stroke.
scenes.visual: Five separate stimulus icons appear in turn, each with its own panel: press, motion, vibration, bent hair, stroking brush.
scenes.narration: Like overlapping filters, each class favours its own part. A held press. Skin motion. Fast vibration. The slightest bend of a hair. A slow stroke.

scenes.tts: The ending, with the neuron's own properties, shapes what a class responds to best. Axon size and myelin set how fast the report travels.
scenes.visual: An ending and a neuron glow beside each icon; below, three axons of different thickness and myelin labelled Aβ, Aδ and C, with arrows of different lengths.
scenes.narration: The ending, with the neuron's own properties, shapes what a class responds to best. Axon size and myelin set how fast the report travels.

scenes.tts: Why split at all? The recorded classes are complementary. One keeps reporting a held press. Another catches fast vibrations too small for the rest.
scenes.visual: Two schematic sensitivity profiles side by side, labelled schematic: SA I sustained under a held press, PC over fast vibration.
scenes.narration: Why split at all? The recorded classes are complementary. One keeps reporting a held press. Another catches fast vibrations too small for the rest.

scenes.tts: No class reports the whole touch. So the nervous system reads the pattern across the classes that share the skin.
scenes.visual: All rasters light together; a bracket gathers them into one pattern.
scenes.narration: No class reports the whole touch. So the nervous system reads the pattern across the classes that share the skin.

scenes.tts: This extends the Touch and pain rule. Endings help decide what a line can report, even within one sense.
scenes.visual: The Touch and pain table returns, with an ending drawn behind each box.
scenes.narration: This extends the Touch and pain rule. Endings help decide what a line can report, even within one sense.

scenes.tts: One press, several reports. Next, mouse hairy skin, where three classes can share a single hair.
scenes.visual: A mouse hair with three endings around it fades in.
scenes.narration: One press, several reports. Next, mouse hairy skin, where three classes can share a single hair.
